text:
oliver: Heads up — after the RBAC refactor rollout at 08:10, gpu-job-controller started returning 403s for a subset of sandbox namespaces. noticed ~30 failing pods, looks like rolebinding resolution changed order.

maya: saw that too, reproducible in staging with `kubectl auth can-i` returning no for `create pods/exec`.

sam: can you paste the failing RoleBinding? I want to check subjects.

oliver: here's the trimmed binding that failed:
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: gpu-runner-binding
  namespace: sandbox-qa
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: gpu-job-runner-v2
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: gpu-runner-sa
  namespace: ci
```

li: aha — subject namespace != binding namespace. The previous controller implicitly allowed cross-namespace SA for this controller; new least-priv change tightened that. That explains the 403s.

carla: we intentionally tightened cross-namespace binds in the refactor. But we didn't migrate the gpu controllers to use namespace-aligned SAs.

maya: quick triage plan: 1) rollback refactor for controllers (canary) 2) add a migration task to either: a) create namespace-scoped SAs for gpu controllers, or b) add explicit RoleBindings per target namespace with narrow perms 3) adjust audit sampling so we can see how many cross-ns binds exist.

sam: agree. Suggest we avoid wide Role creations. Proposal: create a ClusterRole with no wildcard verbs and then RoleBindings in each namespace that reference it. That keeps permissions explicit.

oliver: temporary mitigation: re-apply legacy RoleBinding behavior in a glue Job that creates per-namespace RoleBinding for `gpu-runner-sa` across the affected namespaces. I'll open a PR for the job.

carla: also, FYI — KMS access path: the deploys were failing for a subset because the controller's KMS envelope key permission was namespace-scoped. After the refactor the controller no longer had `decrypt` on the KMS key for those namespaces. two separate failures converged.

li: can we add an audit log alert rule for KMS decrypt denies + pod create 403s within 1m? That would have surfaced this sooner.

maya: yes — I'll add a Detection rule: `audit.kms.decrypt == \"DENIED\" AND kubernetes.request.verb == \"create\" AND kubernetes.resource == \"pods\"` with lookback 1m. Also increase retention for those audit events for 72h.

deploy-bot: deploy reported: rollback started for rollout/eng-security-rbac-v2 to revision 2026.

sam: For the migration task, I'll draft the per-namespace RoleBinding generator (go binary) that reads a CSV of target namespaces and emits RoleBinding YAML. Will add an opt-in flag and a dry-run.

oliver: action items:
- oliver: PR for glue Job to recreate per-namespace RoleBindings (ASAP)
- sam: generator binary + PR to infra repo (EOD)
- maya: detection rule + audit retention change (infra-detection)
- li: verify KMS keypolicy and open a request to add decrypt for controller principal where appropriate
- carla: coordinate communications with oncall and affected teams

carla: thanks — will notify oncall and customers affected. tagging @sec-sre to watch for followups.

maya: one follow-up design note: long-term we should avoid cross-namespace SAs for privileged controllers. Either adopt namespace-local controllers or explicit per-namespace bindings created via a controlled automation. I'll add to the least-priv initiative board.

oliver: thanks everyone, monitoring now. I'll post updates if anything else crops up.
